unit.title: Maintain a safe, clean and efficient work environment

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a 'hazard' in the salon?
options: The chance that someone will be hurt by something
A form you fill in after an accident has happened
Anything that could cause harm, such as a wet floor
A person who is trained to give first aid at work

questions.stem: What does 'risk' mean?
options: Anything at all in the salon that is made of glass
The cost of fixing a broken piece of equipment
The name of the person who reports a hazard
How likely it is that a hazard will cause harm

questions.stem: You notice a cracked floor tile at the edge of the basin area. What should you do?
options: Warn others, mark the area and report it to the supervisor
Cover it with a towel and say nothing until it gets worse
Try to glue it back in place with nail glue from the shelf
Wait to see if a client trips on it before you report it

questions.stem: What is the first step of a risk assessment?
options: Write the report and then file it away for the year
Buy new equipment for the whole salon at once
Look around and find the hazards in the work area
Wait until an accident happens and then act

questions.stem: Why should hazards be reported even when no one has been hurt yet?
options: So that the person who caused it can be punished
So that the salon can close for the rest of the day
So that clients can be told to stay away from the salon
So that they can be fixed before an accident happens

questions.stem: What is a 'near miss'?
options: A client who arrives just after the salon has closed
An event that could have caused injury but did not
A booking that was nearly made twice for one stylist
A product that nearly ran out before it was reordered

questions.stem: What is the difference between disinfecting and sterilising?
options: Disinfecting kills most germs; sterilising kills all of them
Disinfecting is done with heat; sterilising is done only with soap
Disinfecting is for floors; sterilising is for hands and skin
They are the same thing, just two names for one process

questions.stem: Which piece of equipment sterilises metal tools using steam under pressure?
options: An ultraviolet (UV) cabinet
An autoclave
A hood dryer
A hair steamer

questions.stem: What is a UV cabinet used for in a salon?
options: Storing tools that are already cleaned and disinfected
Sterilising dirty tools that still have hair on them
Drying wet towels quickly between one client and the next
Warming oils and creams before a massage

questions.stem: Why must tools be cleaned before they are put into disinfectant?
options: Hair and dirt stop the disinfectant reaching the surface
Disinfectant only works on tools that are bone dry
Cleaning makes the disinfectant smell more pleasant
Dirty tools make the disinfectant turn a darker colour

questions.stem: How should a disinfectant solution be prepared and used?
options: Mixed extra strong and kept for a whole month
Mixed by guess, with any amount of water
Mixed and timed as the maker's label says
Mixed with a second cleaner to make it stronger

questions.stem: What is the correct way to wash your hands?
options: Rinse quickly under cold water and dry on your uniform
Wipe them on a damp towel shared by all the staff
Use hand cream only, as it kills all germs on the skin
Lather with soap for about 20 seconds, rinse and dry

questions.stem: A client's skin is nicked and bleeds a little during a service. What should you do?
options: Carry on, as a small cut will stop bleeding on its own
Wipe the blood off with the client's towel and carry on
Put some styling gel on the cut to seal it quickly
Put on gloves, give first aid and clean the area safely

questions.stem: Why must razors and blades never be shared or reused between clients?
options: They can pass on infections carried in the blood
They become blunt after one use and look untidy
They cost less when each one is used only once
They rust as soon as they touch any hair at all

questions.stem: Where should a used razor blade be put?
options: In the general waste bin, wrapped in a paper towel
In the drawer, so it can be used again later
In a sharps box that is puncture-proof
In the recycling bin with the empty bottles

questions.stem: How should cut hair on the salon floor be dealt with?
options: Left until closing time so that it is all swept at once
Pushed under the station where clients cannot see it
Blown away with a hair dryer towards the door
Swept up after each client and put in a covered bin

questions.stem: How should empty chemical containers and leftover mixed chemicals be got rid of?
options: Poured down the basin with hot water to wash them away
Kept on the shelf in case they are needed another day
As the maker's instructions and the local rules say
Burned outside the salon in a metal drum

questions.stem: Where should salon chemicals such as relaxers and peroxide be stored?
options: On a sunny windowsill so the labels are easy to read
In a cool, dry, locked place, in their own labelled containers
In empty drink bottles, which are easier to carry around the salon
On the top shelf above the basins where they can be reached

questions.stem: What is a safety data sheet (SDS) used for?
options: To list the prices of all the salon's chemical products
To record the hours worked by each member of staff
To show the client how her finished style should look
To give the hazards, safe use and first aid for a product

questions.stem: Why should you never mix different cleaning chemicals, such as bleach and an ammonia cleaner?
options: They can react and give off a dangerous gas
They will clean twice as well and waste product
They will change colour and stain the floor tiles
They will turn into plain water and do nothing

questions.stem: Relaxer splashes into a stylist's eye. What should be done first?
options: Rinse with plenty of clean, running water and get help
Rub the eye hard with a dry towel to get the cream out
Put a little conditioner in the eye to soothe it, then wait
Keep the eye closed and finish the client before resting

questions.stem: Which protective clothing should a stylist wear when mixing and applying a relaxer?
options: A paper mask and open-toed sandals
Gloves and a protective apron
A cotton cap and rubber boots
Sunglasses and a long necklace

questions.stem: Why should the salon be well ventilated when chemicals and sprays are used?
options: So that the products dry faster on the client's hair
So that clients outside can smell the salon's products
So that fumes do not build up and harm people's breathing
So that the air conditioning can be switched off all day

questions.stem: How can stylists help prevent sore, cracked skin on their hands from products and wet work?
options: Wash the hands often in very hot water, with no drying
Use bare hands with chemicals so the skin toughens up
Wear gloves, then dry the hands well and moisturise them
Keep the hands damp all day so the skin does not crack

questions.stem: What should you do before cleaning a blow-dryer or flat iron?
options: Leave it switched on so you can see that it still works
Spray it with water to cool it down more quickly
Clean it while hot so the product comes off easily
Switch it off, unplug it and let it cool down first

questions.stem: Why should you not plug many tools into one socket using adaptors?
options: It makes the tools heat up more slowly than usual
It can overload the socket and cause a fire
It uses up the electricity faster in the meter
It makes the cables too short to reach the chair

questions.stem: Who should repair a faulty hood dryer?
options: Any stylist who has a screwdriver at hand
A qualified person, as the salon arranges
The client who reported that it was not working
The newest trainee, to gain some experience

questions.stem: During a thunderstorm the power goes off and comes back on. A hood dryer now smells of burning. What should you do?
options: Leave it on to see if the smell goes away after a while
Spray it with water to cool it down and stop the smell
Switch it off, unplug it, label it and report it
Turn it to a lower heat and carry on with the client

questions.stem: What three things does a fire need to burn?
options: Water, wind and smoke
Heat, fuel and oxygen
Light, sound and gas
Paper, plastic and metal

questions.stem: Which of these is suitable for putting out a small fire in electrical equipment?
options: A carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguisher
A water extinguisher
A wet towel thrown over the dryer
A bucket of water from the basin

questions.stem: What is the safe way to treat aerosol cans such as hairspray?
options: Keep them away from heat and flames and never pierce them
Store them on top of the hood dryer to keep them warm
Throw the empty cans onto a fire to get rid of them more quickly
Spray them near a lit candle to check that they work

questions.stem: When the fire alarm sounds, what should staff do?
options: Finish the service first, then leave if there is smoke
Collect all of their personal belongings before they leave
Guide clients out by the nearest exit to the meeting point
Hide in the store room and wait until the alarm stops

questions.stem: Why must fire exits be kept clear?
options: So that deliveries can be left there for collection
So that everyone can get out quickly in an emergency
So that the cleaner has somewhere to store the mops
So that clients can smoke there between services

questions.stem: Which is the best way to prevent trips in the salon?
options: Leave bags and boxes in walkways where you can see them
Run long cables across the floor between the stations
Keep the lights low so that the salon looks calm
Keep walkways clear and cables tucked away safely

questions.stem: How should you lift a heavy box of stock from the floor?
options: Bend over at the waist, keeping your legs straight, and lift fast
Twist your body to the side as you lift it up
Bend your knees, keep your back straight and hold it close
Lift it above your head to carry it to the shelf

questions.stem: How can a stylist avoid back and neck pain while working on clients?
options: Keep the client's chair as low as it will go all day
Stand on one leg and lean over the client's head
Adjust the chair height and stand with weight even
Work through lunch so the day finishes sooner

questions.stem: Where should first aid supplies be kept?
options: Locked in the owner's car so they are not used up
In a marked first aid box that staff can reach easily
In each stylist's handbag, so they can take them home
In the store room behind the boxes of chemicals

questions.stem: A trainee slips and hurts her wrist. After first aid, what else must be done?
options: Nothing, as long as she says she feels better
Record the accident in the accident book or report form
Tell her to keep it secret so the salon is not blamed
Ask the clients if any of them saw it happen

questions.stem: Why should stylists wear closed, flat shoes at work?
options: To protect the feet from spills, dropped tools and slips
To look taller and more professional to the salon's clients
To keep the feet cool in the heat of the salon
To match the colour of the salon's uniform

questions.stem: What does 'clean as you go' mean?
options: Clean only when the supervisor is watching you
Leave all cleaning until the end of the week
Ask the client to tidy up before she leaves
Tidy and clean during and after each task

questions.stem: Which is a good way to save electricity in the salon?
options: Leave all the dryers on all day so they are always warm
Keep the front door open with the air conditioning on
Run the washing machine with only one towel in it
Switch off and unplug tools when they are not being used

questions.stem: A tap at the basin keeps dripping. What should you do?
options: Report it so it can be fixed, as it wastes water and money
Put a towel under the tap so that no one hears the drip
Turn the tap on full to flush the drip out of the pipe
Leave it, because a little dripping water costs nothing

questions.stem: How can the salon prevent pests such as cockroaches, ants and rats?
options: Leave food in the staff area overnight for the cleaner
Keep the bins open so they are easier to empty
Spray strong insect spray over the clients' chairs
Keep the salon clean, close bins and store food away

questions.stem: How should towels used on clients be washed?
options: Rinsed by hand in cold water and hung over the chairs
Washed hot with detergent, then dried fully
Shaken out and folded for use the next day
Washed with the staff's own clothes at home

questions.stem: Why should each tool and product have its own place at the station?
options: So that each stylist can lock their tools away from others
So that the station looks full and busy to the clients
So that things are quick to find and nothing is left out
So that the supervisor can count them at the end of the day

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters PPE stand for?
What type of germ causes ringworm?
What type of germ, much smaller than bacteria, causes colds, flu and warts?
What do we call the length of time a tool must stay in a disinfectant for it to work?
What sign should be put out after the floor has been mopped?
What is the name of the skin condition, with red, dry, itchy and cracked skin, that stylists often get from chemicals and wet work?
What is the name for a person trained to give first aid at work?
In Jamaica, what is the frequency of the mains electricity supply, in hertz?
What is the name for germs that can cause disease?
What is the name of the stock rule that the oldest products are used before the newest?
A disinfectant must be mixed 1 part to 9 parts water. How much disinfectant do you need to make 1 litre (1000 ml) of solution?
A cable runs across a walkway. What kind of hazard is this?
What must every chemical container in the salon have on it, so that people know what is inside?
What word describes the daily work of keeping the salon clean, tidy and in order?
When you carry scissors, which way should the points face?

essays.stem: Explain the difference between a hazard and a risk. Describe five hazards found in a salon and say how each one can be controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: A hazard is anything that could cause harm. A risk is how likely it is that the hazard will cause harm, and how bad the harm could be. A wet floor near the basins is a hazard; the risk is high if it is not wiped up and people walk there. Five salon hazards are: water or hair on the floor, controlled by wiping and sweeping at once and using a wet floor sign; trailing cables, controlled by keeping cables tidy and out of walkways; chemicals such as relaxers and peroxide, controlled by storing them locked and labelled, wearing gloves and following the maker's instructions; hot tools, controlled by resting them on heat-proof stands and unplugging them after use; and heavy boxes of stock, controlled by lifting with bent knees and getting help. All hazards should be reported to the supervisor and recorded.
markingPoints: Correct meaning of hazard
Correct meaning of risk, with an example
Names five sensible salon hazards
Gives a suitable control for each hazard
Mentions reporting or recording hazards

essays.stem: Describe how to clean, disinfect and store combs, brushes and metal tools after use, and explain where sterilising fits in.
essays.modelAnswer: First I put on gloves. I remove all hair from combs and brushes with a comb or brush cleaner. I wash the tools in warm water with detergent, scrubbing to remove product and dirt, then rinse them. Cleaning comes first, because hair and dirt stop the disinfectant reaching the surface. Next I put them fully under a disinfectant solution, mixed as the maker says, for the right contact time. I make fresh solution as often as the maker says, or when it looks dirty. I take the tools out, rinse them if the maker says so, and dry them with a clean towel. I store them in a clean, closed container or a UV cabinet so they stay clean. Sterilising kills all germs, including spores, for example in an autoclave. It is used for metal tools that may have touched blood or broken skin, if the salon has the equipment. Single-use items are thrown away.
markingPoints: Wears gloves and removes all hair
Washes with detergent and rinses before disinfecting, with the reason
Uses disinfectant mixed and timed as the maker says, renewed regularly
Dries and stores tools in a clean, closed container or UV cabinet
Explains sterilising (all germs, autoclave) and when it is used; single-use items thrown away

essays.stem: Explain how salon chemicals should be stored, handled and disposed of safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Chemicals such as relaxers, colours, peroxide, perm solutions and cleaning products must be stored in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place, out of direct sunlight, in a locked cupboard away from clients and children. They are kept in their own labelled containers and never put into drink bottles. Heavy containers go on low shelves. Lids must be closed tightly. The safety data sheet for each product is kept where staff can find it. When handling chemicals, I read the label and follow the maker's instructions. I wear gloves and an apron, and eye protection if there is a splash risk. I work in a ventilated area and never mix different products or brands. I mix only what is needed. I wipe up spills at once. To dispose of chemicals, I follow the maker's instructions and the local rules. I do not pour large amounts down the drain, and I rinse empty containers if the label says so before putting them out.
markingPoints: Stored cool, dry, ventilated, out of sunlight and locked away
Kept in labelled original containers with lids closed, heavy items low, SDS available
Handles with gloves and apron, following the maker's instructions, in ventilation
Never mixes products, and mixes only what is needed
Disposes as the maker and local rules say, not large amounts down the drain

essays.stem: Describe how you would deal safely with a chemical spill on the salon floor.
essays.modelAnswer: First I warn people nearby and keep clients and staff away from the spill, so that no one slips or steps in it. I put out a warning sign. I find out what the chemical is from the label, and check its safety data sheet for how to clean it up. I open windows or switch on the extractor fan if there are fumes. I put on gloves and an apron, and eye protection if needed. I soak up the spill with paper towels or the spill kit the salon keeps, working from the outside in so it does not spread. I put the used towels in a sealed bag and dispose of them as the data sheet and the Centre's rules say. I then wash the area with water and detergent and dry it fully. I wash my hands. Finally, I report the spill to the supervisor and record it, and tell them if any product has run low.
markingPoints: Warns others, keeps people away and puts out a sign
Checks the label and safety data sheet, and ventilates
Wears gloves and apron (and eye protection if needed)
Soaks up from the outside in, bags the waste and disposes of it correctly
Washes and dries the area, washes hands and reports the spill

essays.stem: Explain how to use electrical equipment such as dryers, irons and steamers safely in the salon.
essays.modelAnswer: Before using any electrical tool, I check it: the plug must not be cracked, the cable must not be split or have bare wires, and the casing must not be damaged. I never use a tool with wet hands or near water, and I keep tools away from the basins. I plug each tool into its own socket and do not overload sockets with adaptors. I keep cables tidy and out of walkways so no one trips, and I do not wrap cables tightly around hot tools. I follow the maker's instructions for each tool. After use, I switch it off, unplug it by the plug, not the cable, and let it cool on a heat-proof stand before putting it away or cleaning it. If a tool sparks, smells of burning or does not work properly, I switch it off, unplug it, label it 'Do not use' and report it. Only a qualified person should repair it. Equipment should be checked regularly as the salon arranges.
markingPoints: Checks the plug, cable and casing before use
No wet hands or water nearby; keeps tools away from basins
Does not overload sockets; keeps cables tidy and out of walkways
Switches off and unplugs by the plug after use, and lets tools cool
Labels and reports faults; repair only by a qualified person

essays.stem: Describe how a salon can prevent fires, and what staff should do if a fire breaks out.
essays.modelAnswer: To prevent fires, the salon keeps the three parts of the fire triangle (heat, fuel and oxygen) apart. Staff switch off and unplug tools after use, rest hot tools on heat-proof stands, and never overload sockets. Aerosols such as hairspray are kept away from heat and flames and never pierced. Towels, paper and chemicals are stored away from heaters and hot tools. Faulty equipment is reported. Rubbish is emptied daily. Fire exits are kept clear and extinguishers are checked. If a fire breaks out, the person who finds it raises the alarm and calls the fire service. Staff stop work, switch off equipment if it is safe, and guide all clients out by the nearest exit to the meeting point, without stopping for belongings. A small fire may be tackled only by someone trained, with the right extinguisher, such as carbon dioxide for electrical fires, and only if there is a safe way out. No one goes back in. The supervisor checks that everyone is out.
markingPoints: Explains the fire triangle or keeping heat away from fuel
Gives at least three prevention steps (tools off, aerosols, storage, exits clear)
Raises the alarm and calls the fire service
Guides clients out by the nearest exit to the meeting point, leaving belongings
Only trained staff use the right extinguisher, and only with a safe way out; checks everyone is out

essays.stem: Explain how stylists can protect their own health at work. Include posture, hands and skin, breaks and personal hygiene.
essays.modelAnswer: Stylists stand for many hours, so posture matters. They should adjust the client's chair so they can work with a straight back and relaxed shoulders, stand with their weight on both feet and move their feet instead of twisting. Lifting should be done with bent knees, and heavy loads shared. To protect hands and skin, stylists wear gloves for chemicals and wet work, dry their hands well and use a moisturiser, to prevent dermatitis. Cuts on the hands are covered with a waterproof plaster. Breaks are important: short rests, stretching, eating and drinking water help prevent tiredness, strain and mistakes. For personal hygiene, stylists wash their hands before and after each client, wear a clean uniform each day, tie back long hair, keep nails short and clean, and wear closed, flat shoes. They should stay at home and tell the supervisor if they have an infection that could spread to clients.
markingPoints: Good posture: chair height, straight back, weight even, safe lifting
Hands and skin: gloves, drying, moisturising, cuts covered
Regular breaks, stretching, food and water
Personal hygiene: hand washing, clean uniform, hair tied back, short nails
Closed flat shoes, and staying home with an infection

essays.stem: Describe what should happen when someone has an accident in the salon, from first aid to reporting.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the area is made safe so no one else is hurt, for example by switching off a tool or wiping up a spill. The person is kept calm and still, and the first aider is called. The first aider wears gloves if there is blood and gives first aid from the first aid box, such as cooling a burn with cool running water or covering a cut. If the injury is serious, someone calls an ambulance at once. The supervisor is told. When the person has been cared for, the accident is written in the accident book or on the report form: the date, time and place, the name of the person, what happened, the injury, the first aid given and who saw it. The first aid box is restocked. The supervisor looks at why the accident happened and what can be changed to stop it happening again. Near misses are reported in the same way.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe first
Calls the first aider, who gives suitable first aid with gloves
Calls an ambulance for serious injuries and tells the supervisor
Records the accident fully in the accident book or report form
Finds the cause and changes things to prevent it; near misses reported too

essays.stem: Explain how a salon can save electricity, water and products, and why this matters.
essays.modelAnswer: To save electricity, staff switch off and unplug dryers, irons and steamers when they are not in use, and switch off lights and fans in empty rooms. Doors and windows are kept closed when the air conditioning is on. The washing machine is run with full loads. To save water, taps are turned off between rinses, and dripping taps or leaking pipes are reported and fixed quickly. To save products, staff use the right amount for the hair's length and thickness, close lids after use and store products as the maker says so they do not spoil. Stock is checked and the oldest is used first, so nothing goes out of date. Saving matters because electricity and water bills in Jamaica are high, so waste costs the salon money and can affect prices and wages. Saving also protects the environment, and a tidy, well-run salon gives clients a good impression.
markingPoints: Electricity: switch off and unplug, lights off, doors closed with air conditioning, full loads
Water: taps off, leaks reported and fixed
Products: right amounts, lids closed, stored correctly
Stock rotation so nothing goes out of date
Explains why: cost, environment and the salon's image

essays.stem: Describe a daily cleaning routine for the salon: what is cleaned, when, and with what.
essays.modelAnswer: At opening, staff check that the salon is clean and dry, wipe the stations and mirrors, and put out clean towels and gowns. After each client, the stylist sweeps up hair and puts it in a covered bin. Combs, brushes and clips are cleaned and disinfected. The chair, armrests and counter are wiped with disinfectant, and used towels go into the laundry bin. The basin is cleared of hair and wiped with disinfectant. During the day, staff clean as they go: spills are wiped up at once, bins are emptied when full and the toilet and staff area are checked. At closing, all tools are cleaned and disinfected, basins, chairs and work surfaces are washed and disinfected, the floor is swept and mopped with a wet floor sign out, bins are emptied and closed, laundry is washed hot and dried fully, and products are closed and put away. Gloves are worn for cleaning chemicals, and the maker's instructions are followed.
markingPoints: Opening checks: clean, dry stations and fresh towels
After each client: hair swept, tools disinfected, chair and basin wiped, towels to laundry
During the day: clean as you go, spills wiped up, bins emptied
Closing: surfaces disinfected, floor mopped with a sign, bins emptied, laundry washed hot
Uses suitable products with gloves, following the maker's instructions

practical1.title: Hazard check and risk assessment of the training salon
practical1.brief: Before the task, the assessor sets out some hazards in the Centre's training salon, such as a trailing cable, water on the floor, an unlabelled bottle, a blocked fire exit, an open chemical, a hot tool left on a chair and a heavy box in a walkway. Your group of 4 or 5 shares the salon into areas (reception, styling stations, basins, store room and staff area), and each member checks one area. Each member photographs each hazard found and records it on the group's risk assessment form: the hazard, who could be harmed, how likely and how serious, and the control. Then, with the assessor's permission, each member puts the controls in place in their area and photographs it again. Together, make an A3 safety poster of the five most important salon safety rules to put up in the salon. Each member presents their area to the assessor. Hand in once for the whole group with the photos, the form and the poster.
materials: Blank risk assessment forms with columns for hazard, who could be harmed, likelihood, severity and control
A wet floor sign, cable covers or tape, labels and a marker
A3 card or chart paper and coloured markers
A phone or tablet for photos
photos: Each hazard as it was found
The same place after the control was put in place
The finished safety poster on display
Each member pointing out a hazard in their area (hands and area only, no faces)
checklist: Found the hazards in their own area
Recorded each hazard with who could be harmed and how likely and serious it is
Gave a suitable control for each hazard
Put the controls in place safely and with permission
Handled chemicals and hot or electrical items safely, with gloves where needed
Wrote at least one clear rule for the poster
Explained their area and its hazards clearly to the assessor
safety: Do not touch hot tools; ask the assessor to switch off and unplug any electrical item
Wear gloves before moving any chemical container, and do not open it
Lift boxes with bent knees and a straight back, or ask for help
Report anything that looks like a real fault, not part of the task, to the assessor at once

practical2.title: Clean, disinfect and reset the salon, and check chemical storage
practical2.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5 in the Centre's training salon at the end of a practical session. Share the jobs so that every member does each of these at least once: (1) clean and disinfect the combs, brushes and clips from one station, using a disinfectant mixed to the maker's instructions, and store them correctly; (2) clean and disinfect one basin and one styling station; (3) sort the waste into general waste, a sharps box (using the empty training blades the assessor gives) and bags for laundry; (4) check the chemical store: every container labelled, lids closed, heavy items low, oldest stock at the front, and the safety data sheets in place; (5) fill in the salon cleaning log with the time, the job and your name. Photograph each area before and after. Hand in once for the whole group with the photos and the completed cleaning log.
materials: Disinfectant with the maker's instructions, a measuring jug and a covered container
Detergent, brushes for cleaning tools, cloths and paper towels
A sharps box and empty training blades from the assessor
General waste bags and a laundry bin
The salon cleaning log and pens
A mop, bucket and wet floor sign
A phone or tablet for photos
photos: Each station and basin before cleaning
The disinfectant being measured and mixed
Tools in the disinfectant, then stored in a covered container
Each station and basin after cleaning
The waste sorted into general waste, sharps box and laundry
checklist: Wore gloves and an apron for cleaning and disinfectant
Removed hair and washed tools before disinfecting them
Mixed the disinfectant as the maker says and used the right contact time
Cleaned and disinfected the basin and station fully
Put blades only in the sharps box and sorted the other waste correctly
Checked labels, lids, shelf position and stock order in the chemical store
Mopped safely with a wet floor sign out
Filled in the cleaning log clearly
safety: Never mix cleaning chemicals; use one product at a time as the label says
Keep the area ventilated while using disinfectant
Handle blades by the blunt edge and never push them into a full sharps box
Put out a wet floor sign and keep others away until the floor is dry
